Home/Insights/Technical Seo Audit Checklist

What Should an Agency Technical SEO Audit Include?

An acceptance checklist for audits that teams can actually implement.

Practical guide · Evaluation criteria, examples and next steps

An audit should tell the developer which URLs to test, what failure to reproduce and how to confirm the fix. A severity score without that trail is not a ticket.

Crawlability and indexation

Start with the URLs search engines can find and those that should appear in results. Check robots directives, XML sitemaps, indexability signals, pagination and parameter behavior, and samples from Search Console. State when a finding comes from a crawl versus live search data.

  • Blocked or accidentally noindexed pages
  • Canonical and duplicate URL patterns
  • Redirect chains and error responses

Rendering, navigation, and site architecture

Inspect whether important links and page content remain discoverable when JavaScript is involved. Review menu paths, orphaned pages, depth, internal linking, structured data, and template-level issues. A site-wide bug often matters more than a one-page typo.

  • Rendered HTML checks
  • Internal-link destination integrity
  • Site structure by template

Performance with honest context

Separate laboratory performance diagnostics from field data. Report the device, source, time period, and template. Core Web Vitals can inform prioritization, but a faster score alone is not a guarantee of higher rankings or more conversions.

  • Largest Contentful Paint conditions
  • Interaction responsiveness and layout stability
  • Image, script, and caching opportunities

Business relevance and prioritization

An audit becomes useful when the findings are ranked by impact, confidence, effort, number of affected pages, and dependencies. The document should explain why one fix comes before another, not simply display severity labels generated by a tool.

  • Priority rationale
  • Assigned implementation owner
  • Estimated dependency and review point

Verification and handoff

Every recommendation needs a testable finish. Link to the live change, re-crawl representative pages, and record what improved, what remains, and where external factors limit confidence. Never mark a fix complete just because an email was sent.

  • Before/after evidence
  • Implementation date and URL
  • Reviewer signoff or outstanding blocker

Sample audit issue record and re-test procedure

A useful audit finding is reproducible. Suppose a priority service URL has two consecutive redirects before the canonical destination. The issue ticket should expose the response sequence rather than just label the page “high priority.”

Example or checkpointRecommended actionReview or acceptance
EvidenceRequest URL, redirect status chain, final destination, crawl timestampAnother reviewer can reproduce the observation
Risk assessmentInternal linking to old URL may waste hops or confuse canonical targetingPriority depends on page importance and actual crawl impact
Recommended actionUpdate internal links to the canonical destination; review redirect rulesDeveloper has exact links or templates to change
AcceptanceRe-crawl sample URLs and inspect final canonical responseDocument before/after proof and remaining exceptions

High impact is an assessment, not a guarantee. Prioritize across affected templates, expected search value and implementation cost, then retest after publishing.

Download: Technical audit issue tracker (CSV)

Relevant reference material

  • Google redirects guidance
  • Google canonical guidance

Frequently asked questions

Should the audit include every tool warning?

Tool exports can be attached, but the executive audit should focus on validated and prioritized findings.

Can a technical audit guarantee traffic growth?

No. The audit removes or explains barriers; demand, content, and competition remain relevant.

Who implements the changes?

The scope should name whether the SEO agency, developer, or client implements each recommendation.

An audit issue a developer can actually close

Hypothetical example: a category template generates non-canonical indexable URLs. An actionable audit records the URL pattern, the response and indexability signals, the intended canonical, and a retest after deployment.

Evaluation elementPractical check
ObservationSpecific URL pattern and how the crawler finds it
ReproductionHTTP status, canonical, robots and internal link evidence
Proposed fixApproved canonical policy and relevant template changes
RetestConfirm expected URLs and signals after publishing
ClosureAttach dated validation rather than relying on a completion label

In this guide

Crawlability and indexationRendering, navigation, and site architecturePerformance with honest contextBusiness relevance and prioritizationVerification and handoff

Use reproducible findings, not the number of warnings in a crawl export.

What SEO Metrics Belong in a White-Label Client Report?

Metrics, context, and narrative for reports your agency can confidently send.

Practical guide · Evaluation criteria, examples and next steps

An agency report must separate what shipped, what search performance did and which decisions remain open. Mixing those three stories makes the report impossible to act on.

Start with what the client is trying to achieve

A local service client cares about qualified enquiries, while a publisher may prioritize engaged organic visits. Reporting should choose a small set of decision-useful measures rather than include every available chart. Define the source and conversion meaning before the first report.

  • Business goal and measurement period
  • Primary conversions and attribution limitations
  • Priority pages and services

Use rankings as diagnostic evidence

Keyword positions should include location, device, tool, search engine, and date. Show distribution across position bands and changes for agreed keywords, not a handpicked list of only winners. Group brand terms separately where possible.

  • Tracked keyword coverage
  • Positions by segment
  • Queries newly visible or declining

Connect search performance to landing pages

  • Engaged landing-page visits
  • Calls, forms, demos, or bookings where reliable

Report delivery evidence

Clients deserve to see what work was completed. Link to approved pages, release notes, issue records, content briefs, and profile changes. Separate proposed, approved, live, verified, and blocked statuses. This reduces the temptation to equate activity count with impact.

  • Completed deliverables
  • Work waiting on approval
  • Next cycle priorities with owner

End with a decision

A good report states what changed, what is uncertain, and what should happen next. If a page gained impressions but not qualified leads, the next step might be a conversion review. If indexing remains blocked, the next step is technical implementation, not more blog posts.

  • Interpretation of movement
  • Risks and dependencies
  • Actions for the next review

Example monthly report with decision context

Separate delivered work from observed search metrics. If rankings move but the content release is still blocked, a client should be able to see both facts without implying a causal link.

  1. Separate branded and non-branded query changes and keep the filters visible.
  2. Explain affected landing pages and work completed, not only aggregate traffic.

Choose the reporting order based on the client objective, but show the relationship between visibility and useful business outcomes.

Yes, under agreed brand and approval rules; raw data sources should still be traceable internally.

Is estimated traffic the same as actual visits?

No. Clearly label third-party estimates and keep them separate from analytics measurements.

A report should separate three different questions

Avoid mixing output metrics, search measurements and business outcomes. A clear report explains the difference before it describes the trend.

Make the audit easier to implement

A useful SEO audit is a decision document, not a 70-page export. It tells the business which issues matter, what evidence supports each finding, who can act on it, and how the result will be checked.

Audits are often sold as one-size-fits-all scans. In practice, a migration site, a local-service website, and a large e-commerce catalog face different risks. The scope should reflect business priorities, indexing behavior, content inventory, and access limitations.

From crawls to prioritized recommendations

The audit begins with a short discovery and baseline. We inspect crawlability and indexing, page architecture, search-intent coverage, internal links, performance signals, and available conversion evidence. Findings are prioritized by confidence, impact, scale, implementation effort, and dependencies.

The standard for completion

The audit is useful when an implementer can reproduce a finding, understand the risk and confirm whether the recommended change worked.

  • Executive findings ranked by business priority
  • Detailed issue log with example URLs and reproducible evidence
  • Content and internal-link opportunity map
  • Developer-ready recommendations and owners
  • Re-test protocol and action roadmap

  2. Collect crawl, search, and page evidence
  3. Validate critical findings manually
  4. Deliver an implementable plan and review questions

  • High-priority actions accepted by owners

A useful audit concludes with a responsible owner, due date and acceptance check, not only a score.

Separate defects from opportunities

Not every crawl warning calls for an immediate developer ticket. An outdated non-critical alt attribute and an accidental sitewide noindex are not comparable risks. Group findings by impact, affected template, confidence and implementation dependency.

Prioritize technical issues with evidence

A technical SEO audit is useful only when it helps someone decide what to fix. Large crawls often generate hundreds of warnings, but an engineering team needs a short, defensible queue of issues tied to affected templates, search behavior, and deployment risk.

Technical SEO touches several systems at once: crawling, indexing, JavaScript rendering, canonicalization, migrations, structured data, and Core Web Vitals. Fixes can affect many URLs. We therefore separate an observed symptom from its likely cause and define a re-test before development begins.

Diagnostics and engineering-ready tickets

The process starts with Search Console, crawl evidence, site templates, and release history. Issues are grouped by risk and reach. Each ticket lists an example URL, evidence, suggested action, dependency, priority, and how to verify the fix. Where developers implement changes, the SEO team reviews the deployed result rather than treating a recommendation as completion.

The standard for completion

Close a technical issue only when the deployed page behaves as expected. Capture the previous response, the new response and the date of verification.

  • Redirect, broken-link, and crawl-path findings

  • Migration checklists and pre/post-launch QA

The technical seo handoff in practice

  2. Group symptoms by root cause and affected templates
  3. Agree priority and implementation ownership
  4. Re-crawl samples after the release and log exceptions

  • Developer contact for implementation questions

Schema and speed recommendations follow the same discipline: list the evidence and validation method rather than promising a ranking improvement.

A technical warning is not automatically a priority

An audit can show 400 warnings while the commercial bottleneck is one blocked template. Prioritization should compare affected URLs, actual indexability, revenue relevance, confidence in the diagnosis and whether a fix has an owner.

No. Technical changes remove obstacles and improve site health, but outcomes also depend on content, competition, demand, and other factors.

What white-label SEO means for your agency

White-label SEO works when the client relationship remains with your agency and delivery is still visible, controlled, and accountable. The arrangement is not just unbranded reports. It is a set of boundaries that defines who speaks to the client, who approves changes, and how every task becomes a reviewable output.

An agency can win a new account long before it can hire another full-time specialist. The risk is not only missed deadlines. It is scattered files, inconsistent QA, unexplained rankings, and contractors contacting clients without permission. A documented white-label workflow reduces that friction by keeping responsibilities explicit.

Brief, delivery, approval and handoff

We start with your existing service promise, client-facing formats, tool access, and approval rules. We turn these into a scope with named services, status definitions, and acceptance checks. SEO Outsourcing for Australian Law Firms

Practice-area search is high-stakes. A person looking for help after a workplace dismissal should not land on the same generic page as someone arranging conveyancing. Our proposed SEO service separates those needs, documents claim approvals and keeps the law firm responsible for legal accuracy.

Request an industry SEO scopeExplore Australia sectors

Why search visitors arrive

Law-firm websites often bury distinct matter types under one broad services menu. An intake page can draw traffic without producing suitable enquiries if it fails to say which jurisdictions and matters the lawyers accept. Page templates must not invent accreditation, a “specialist” status, courtroom results or testimonials.

Example search intentInformation the visitor actually needs
Family law consultationClear practice-area scope, jurisdiction, fee process and an appropriate enquiry route
Employment lawyer for unfair dismissalSpecific matter type, who the firm can act for, and time-sensitive next steps reviewed by a lawyer
Commercial contract reviewService boundaries, business audience, document intake and relevant lawyer credentials

The first decisions to get right

Practice-area taxonomy

Map each practice page to real matter types and jurisdiction. Check for conflict with articles, suburb pages and lawyer profiles so two URLs do not compete for the same task.

Lawyer and office accuracy

Review named lawyer bios, practising locations, office hours and intake instructions against the firm’s records. Do not generate office pages for cities without a genuine operation.

Lead quality controls

Separate general enquiry forms from urgent deadlines and confidential document upload. Measure qualified consultations or completed intake forms, not merely clicks on a phone icon.

Editorial review workflow

Attach a named lawyer reviewer and approved source to any new legal explanation. Flag location-specific rules, restrictions and limitation-period statements for professional sign-off.

Example: fewer generic practice pages, better matter routing

A multi-practice firm has a high-traffic “Legal Services” page but poor enquiries for unfair dismissal matters. Instead of cloning that page with suburbs, we would inventory actual employment matters, inspect competing pages and map a dedicated employment-law pathway. The draft would explain eligibility questions, intake steps and legal-review ownership. The firm decides whether the content can be published.

Planning illustration only. No client engagement or performance result is implied.

What an outsourced handoff should contain

StageReviewable outputApproval ownerDefinition of done
AuditIdentify overlapping practice pages and relevant matter-intent queriesSEO lead + solicitorOne approved URL per distinct service intent
ProducePrepare structured draft, internal links and contact-route specificationWriter + lawyer reviewerNo unsupported legal interpretation or credentials
VerifyTest URLs, correct enquiry routing and source linksQA lead + intake coordinatorEnquiry path works and reviewer approval recorded

Australian rules and local facts

Australian solicitors’ advertising must avoid false or misleading claims. In NSW, the Law Society describes specific restrictions on describing lawyers as accredited specialists without appropriate accreditation. Requirements vary by state and legal practice; the firm’s own compliance reviewer has final say.

What to measure beyond keyword rankings

  • Qualified enquiries by matter type
  • Completed consultation-intake forms
  • Search landing pages by practice area

A sensible first pilot

Take one practice area with a real intake team. Assemble the matter-type page map, identify overlapping URLs, draft an approved page brief and test how a potential client actually reaches the right solicitor. Record the lawyer who approves any description of law or professional credentials.

Questions Australian buyers ask

Can outsourced writers publish Australian legal guidance?

They can research and prepare a draft. The law firm must approve legal statements, jurisdictions, credentials and time-sensitive procedural explanations before publishing.

Should each suburb have a lawyer page?

Not unless there is a real service distinction and useful local information. Avoid office claims or profiles for locations where the firm does not operate.

What is a sensible first project?

Audit one practice area, identify competing URLs and repair a single intake pathway before rolling out more content.

Australian reference material

  • Law Society of NSW: advertising legal services
  • Google Business Profile eligibility and service-area rules

What the buyer can inspect

A scoped engagement should leave you with written deliverables and approval responsibilities, not just a promise of more traffic.

  • Practice-area page map with matter-specific FAQs
  • Lawyer-reviewed author/profile checklist
  • Source and claim approval log
  • Conversion event plan separating enquiry types
Discuss this sector →

Build the enquiry around the matter, not the suburb

For a hypothetical unfair-dismissal enquiry, an eligible matter and a timely lawyer response are more useful than an extra city keyword. The firm must confirm jurisdiction and intake capacity.

Before a page is written

Get a lawyer-approved matter list and clarify who may provide advice. Do not use a generic page to imply that every jurisdiction is served.

At the first contact

Offer a neutral consultation route, not a public upload of confidential documents or a promise about deadlines and outcomes.

Proof the pilot worked

SEO Launch QA for Australian Web Design Agencies

Check redirects, crawlability and conversion tracking before a redesigned website goes live. Get a clear list of fixes and responsibilities for your team.

Get a Quote →View sample deliverables

Design teams often own typography, layouts, forms and client approval. SEO problems appear in the gaps: retired URLs disappear without redirects, a development noindex setting travels into production, internal links still point at preview domains, or a contact conversion is never recorded. The SEO handoff should happen before launch, not after a drop in organic traffic.

This is not an offer to create another generic audit PDF. The useful work is a route-by-route launch checklist with a clear developer owner, acceptance test and evidence. If the client has an established site, preserve existing high-value URLs whenever possible. A beautiful redesign is not a reason to change every path.

Which launches need an SEO handoff?

A new business site needs crawlability, clear site architecture and working lead capture. A redesign or CMS migration needs a baseline of the live URLs, their replacement pages, and decisions on every meaningful redirect. A site consolidating services needs checks that the new service architecture still answers the old search intent.

Start by classifying the project: fresh build, same-URL redesign, path-changing migration or domain migration. Those are different risk levels. The higher-risk projects also need a rollback plan, owners for redirect rules and a post-launch crawl scheduled before the development warranty expires.

  • Fresh build: verify approved service URLs, canonical paths, sitemap, schema and enquiries.
  • Same-URL redesign: check accidental content loss, heading hierarchy, core internal links and templates.
  • Path-changing migration: document every important old-to-new URL relationship and test redirects.
  • Domain migration: confirm Search Console properties, canonical destinations and tracking continuity.

A launch checklist your developer can actually close

Assign each check to a route, template or service. For example, testing only the homepage will not reveal that a deeper suburb page redirects through three hops. The SEO reviewer should be able to point to the exact URL, reproduce the problem and identify the final acceptance condition.

CheckEvidence to captureAccept when
Indexing controlsRobots header and meta directive on live templatesApproved pages are indexable; preview pages stay protected
Redirect mapOld URL, new URL, actual response chainPermanent redirects reach the relevant final URL without loops
Forms and eventsTest lead ID, source page and GA4 eventInbox or CRM receives the lead and the event fires once
Mobile templatesRepresentative 390 px and desktop pagesNo clipped CTA, hidden fields, or unusable navigation
Sitemap and canonicalsSubmitted sitemap and rendered canonical tagsApproved URL versions match navigation and response status

Worked handoff: service URLs changed during an Elementor rebuild

Example: An Australian trades website previously used /services/hot-water/ and the redesign team has replaced it with /plumbing/hot-water-systems/. The old page has local search history. The client approves the new menu but nobody has signed off the URL change.

Capture the old URL and its existing inbound and internal links. Confirm the new page serves the same service intent, update the internal navigation, and set a direct permanent redirect from the old page to the chosen new destination. Then crawl both versions after publication. A redirect to the homepage is not an equivalent replacement for a specific service.

Close the ticket only when the old URL reaches the intended final destination, the new page returns 200, its canonical points to itself, the sitemap includes the new path, and the enquiry CTA remains functional. Attach the response chain and a dated retest record.

What stays with the web design agency

The agency owns the final customer sign-off, hosting plan, approved design, access management and DNS decisions. The SEO specialist can write technical tickets, advise on metadata, verify template output and retest changes. Neither party should quietly modify production without the agreed owner approving it.

If the client uses a page builder, define who fixes what before launch: text and internal links may be editable by the content team; redirects, caching rules and structured data may sit with developers or hosting. A checklist with no assigned implementer is not a delivery plan.

  • Agency: client relationship, CMS access, design acceptance, scheduled launch.
  • SEO reviewer: source URL inventory, audit tickets, evidence and post-launch checks.
  • Developer: approved code/configuration fixes, redirects, forms and backups.
  • Client representative: service facts, priority pages, regulatory claims and publication approval.

When not to outsource more work

If the agency has no working backup, no current list of indexed URLs, or no person who can change redirect rules, an expansive SEO retainer will not fix the launch bottleneck. Get those controls in place first. Likewise, do not commission dozens of new suburb pages to replace an established service page just to create more indexed URLs.

A bounded pilot can cover one core service template, one group of redirected URLs and an end-to-end enquiry test. That reveals both implementation quality and whether the delivery handoff fits your agency.

How to measure a successful handoff

Use route-level acceptance, not a promised ranking increase. Record the number of important URLs mapped, redirect exceptions resolved, canonical/indexing errors left open, test conversions received, and post-launch defects reopened. Check Search Console over time for unexpected changes; launch-day positions alone cannot diagnose migration quality.

Request a client-ready evidence pack with the original issue list, approved exceptions, implementation references, final URLs and the person who signed off. This is useful even if a different provider manages ongoing SEO later.

Questions agencies ask before delegating this work

Can an SEO reviewer work alongside our developer without contacting the client?

Yes, when the engagement specifies a white-label workflow. Your agency owns client communication; the reviewer works against assigned tickets and returns unbranded evidence and recommended changes.

Do we need to redirect every old page?

No. Map useful old URLs to relevant new content. Some obsolete pages may properly return 404 or 410; the decision should depend on intent and evidence rather than a blanket homepage redirect.

Can this guarantee rankings after a site rebuild?

No. Launch QA reduces avoidable technical mistakes. Rankings still depend on many factors and can fluctuate during recrawling. The deliverable is verified implementation and a documented monitoring plan.

White-Label Technical SEO Audit Handoffs for Australian Agencies

A crawl export is not a developer brief. This workflow turns technical SEO findings into decisions, assigns owners and defines how the receiving agency will verify each fix.

Get a Quote →View sample deliverables

An agency can find hundreds of crawl issues and still have nothing a developer can close. Broken links, duplicate canonicals and JavaScript rendering warnings are observations. The work is to decide which affected URLs matter, what should happen, who can make the change and how the result will be retested.

Use an audit handoff when your strategist already owns the client account but lacks capacity to triage and write implementation tickets. The output should fit an existing Jira, ClickUp, Zoho Projects or spreadsheet workflow. No client-facing brand transfer is required.

Start with impact, not the audit tool's severity label

A crawler may report 400 redirects, but only a subset may touch priority landing pages or persistent navigation. Conversely, one wrong canonical on a key service page can be more urgent than dozens of isolated image notices. Prioritisation needs impact, reach, reversibility and implementation cost, not simply the number of warnings.

First, define the pages that matter: conversion pages, active products, supported locations and pages with meaningful search exposure. Then group duplicate symptoms by root cause. If a template generates incorrect canonical links across 90 pages, create one template-level decision with a list of affected URLs rather than 90 almost identical tickets.

The evidence contract for each technical ticket

Each issue needs an observed behaviour, a reproduction method and a proposed outcome. Avoid directions such as 'fix technical SEO' or 'improve crawl budget' without a concrete implementation decision. Developers need to know whether the change is in an application template, CMS configuration, JavaScript component or web server.

Retest instructions should be written before the change is assigned. If there is no objective way to say the issue is resolved, the recommendation is probably too vague.

Required fieldWhy it mattersExample
Affected URLsPrevents a vague sitewide ticket/locations/example/ and two linked templates
Observed stateMakes the finding repeatableCanonical points at a retired URL
Approved targetStops accidental redirect or canonical choicesFinal live URL agreed by account owner
Change ownerLocates the actual implementerDeveloper for template; editor for links
Retest and evidenceDefines completionRendered canonical plus recrawl record

Worked example: canonical conflict on a location template

Illustrative scenario only. A multi-location business has a template for regional service pages. A global component inserts a canonical pointing to the national service page on every local landing page. Some pages have distinct local content and should remain separately indexable, while other pages are duplicative.

Before proposing a blanket fix, compare the actual rendered content and intended search need of the affected pages. Decide which versions deserve canonical self-reference and which should consolidate. Document the location pages, the current canonical, the proposed destination and the decision owner. The developer updates the common template only after the account owner approves the set of URLs.

The completed handoff includes rendered source examples before and after, the ticket or commit reference, a crawl confirming expected canonicals, and a separate exception list for pages intentionally consolidated. Simply removing every canonical tag is not an acceptable retest.

Protect the agency's workflow and confidentiality

An outsourced audit team should not assume it can message clients, log into billing systems or publish to production. Agree a read-only evidence collection boundary first. Where authenticated crawling is essential, use named and expiring accounts, documented access and a clear deletion process for exported data.

Deliver findings in the agency's preferred format with neutral wording. If your client has a developer, distinguish recommendations from implemented fixes. Never mark an issue 'fixed' because someone opened a ticket; the status changes after the actual output is checked.

  • Strategist approves business priority and canonical intent.
  • Auditor records evidence, affected URLs, recommendation and reproduction steps.
  • Developer or CMS owner implements only approved changes.
  • Reviewer repeats the test and records any exceptions.

Choose an audit size the team can absorb

Audits often fail because a thick document arrives with no implementation capacity. A better first scope might be the 10 highest-value issues across five page templates, with duplicates consolidated. Once the team has closed those, expand to lower-priority sitewide work.

Separate discovery, technical recommendation, implementation assistance and verification into different work products. This prevents procurement confusion when a quote is for an audit only and the client assumes development is included.

Reporting that explains a decision

The agency account manager should be able to state: the problem, the affected user or search journey, the chosen fix, who approved it and the remaining risk. Track accepted tickets, implemented tickets, retested tickets and unresolved blockers. Search impressions and conversions are useful context, but they do not prove a specific code fix caused a ranking change.

Before sending a white-label report, remove internal tool credentials, private user data and unnecessary screenshots. Keep the evidence needed to verify the fix.

Questions agencies ask before delegating this work

Is a technical audit the same as implementing the fixes?

No. The scope should state separately whether it includes discovery, developer-ready tickets, implementation, and post-change verification. An audit checklist alone is not a deployment.

Can you use our task tracker?

A well-scoped white-label handoff can be prepared for a shared ticketing workflow, subject to agreed access and permissions. Provide required fields and statuses in the first brief.

Should every crawler warning be fixed?

No. Prioritise according to affected pages, actual behaviour, search intent and developer effort. Record deliberate exceptions instead of inflating task counts.

Google Business Profile QA for Australian Agencies

Maps work goes wrong when business facts are guessed, branch locations are invented or review handling is treated as a volume target. This is a verification-led handoff for real Australian locations and service areas.

Get a Quote →View sample deliverables

A Google Business Profile is tied to a real business, not a page a marketer wants to rank. The first job in a white-label local SEO engagement is to establish what the business actually operates: staffed premises, customer-facing hours, service-area boundaries, phone ownership and the account with authority to approve edits.

For agencies managing plumbers, dentists or multi-location brands, the risky mistakes differ. A plumber may need a hidden residential address and accurate dispatch area; a clinic needs practitioner and location review; a merged brand may have historical listings that should not be deleted without a proper transition plan.

Verify the business facts before editing

Request a source-of-truth sheet signed off by the client. It should record the trading name, staffed location or service-area basis, operating hours, actual phone number, website, primary category and person authorised to approve changes. When details vary across directories, do not pick the most common version. Ask the operator which one is current.

Use the public profile and business website as evidence, not a license to create fictional branches. Google's guidelines distinguish genuine staffed offices from virtual offices and mailbox addresses. A marketing agency should not promise extra profiles for suburbs that have no independent eligible location.

  • Physical address and service area match the operating model.
  • Phone and website lead to the business, not a third-party lead-generation destination.
  • Category and services reflect services actually offered.
  • Ownership and manager access are controlled by the business and its authorised representative.

A monthly GBP QA sheet should reveal real changes

An unbranded report should not substitute posting frequency for quality. Each month, log the field checked, observed state, decision, edit approval and follow-up verification. If nothing important changed, report that accurately. A profile with correct hours and a working booking path may need less activity than a profile undergoing a business merger.

ControlFailure exampleAcceptance evidence
Opening hoursHoliday hours copied from an old locationOwner-confirmed hours and live profile capture
Service areaTwelve suburbs claimed without actual coverageDispatch-approved service list and profile settings
Business nameKeyword added to the trading nameTrading name supported by real-world use
ReviewsAuto-generated endorsements or selectively hidden feedbackGenuine review policy; no manipulated ratings
Website linkProfile links to an obsolete or tracking-broken URLWorking destination, attributable enquiry path

Worked example: a plumber serves three suburbs from one depot

Illustrative operating case, not a real client case study. A plumbing company has one staffed depot and serves three nearby suburbs. A marketer proposes three extra Business Profiles and three almost identical suburb landing pages to 'cover the map'.

The safer decision is to confirm that the company has one eligible operating location and accurately defined service areas. Use one genuine Business Profile unless independent, eligible operations support more. On the website, explain the actual services, response hours and dispatch coverage; do not make a fake office page for each suburb.

The acceptance check is a verified profile, current location facts, working phone and service landing pages with substantively different value where appropriate. A ranking-grid screenshot does not override Google's eligibility rules.

Reviews require a separate integrity check

A request for reviews should be directed to genuine customers without offering something in exchange for a positive rating. The ACCC warns against fake or misleading testimonials and selective treatment of reviews. For regulated health services, additional restrictions apply to testimonial use in advertising under Ahpra guidance.

The agency should never fabricate patient stories or repost clinical outcome testimonials onto the practice's own advertising simply because a third-party site displays them. Record when specialist review is required; do not treat a generic reply template as legal clearance.

White-label roles and monthly deliverables

Your account manager stays the client contact. The local SEO delivery team can prepare an issue log, category and service review, verified field suggestions, evidence-backed updates and an unbranded change summary. The business owner should approve sensitive changes, especially name, address, hours and service availability.

A useful pilot is one real profile and one corresponding service page, with a baseline capture and signed-off fact sheet. The quality signal is fewer unresolved factual errors and a reliable enquiry path, not an arbitrary count of posts or citations.

  • Client: confirms legal and operational business details.
  • Agency: approves changes, controls account access and reviews compliance.
  • Delivery reviewer: prepares evidence, change requests and retests.
  • Monthly handoff: completed changes, outstanding disputes, owner approvals and source screenshots.

Which profiles should be excluded from the scope?

Do not build a GBP for an online-only SEO agency with no eligible in-person operating location. Do not create listings for rented mailboxes or unsupported virtual offices. If a client has moved, merged or closed, investigate the appropriate profile treatment rather than erasing historic signals by assumption.

These rules are practical reasons to start with one legitimate profile. They also protect the agency from selling changes it cannot responsibly deliver.

Questions agencies ask before delegating this work

Can we create a Google Business Profile for every suburb?

Not merely because the business serves those suburbs. Eligibility depends on genuine in-person operations and Google’s rules. Service-area configuration is not permission to invent branch offices.

Can we guarantee three-pack rankings with weekly updates?

No. Updates and profile accuracy do not guarantee local ranking positions. Report changes and visibility as separate observations with dates and locations.

What should a white-label GBP report include?

Actual field edits, approved service facts, review-management actions, verification screenshots, problems awaiting owner input and a source-linked view of search visibility.

SEO Content Briefs for Australian Agencies

A keyword list is not a content brief. A strong Australian SEO brief explains who needs the page, which facts the business can substantiate, what the reader must decide and who should review sensitive claims.

Get a Quote →View sample deliverables

An Australian trades service page, a dental treatment page and a B2B software comparison should not come from one article template. Their readers have different concerns, the claims require different evidence and the approval process can vary from a branch manager to a registered practitioner or product owner.

Outsourced content work is most useful when the agency retains voice, source accuracy and publishing approval. The delivery output is a brief that saves the writer research time and saves the reviewer from rebuilding the argument from scratch.

First decide the page's job

A brief should state the search situation in a sentence: a homeowner checking emergency response and fees, a clinic patient asking about treatment suitability, a finance manager comparing software integrations. Group queries by the decision, not by superficial keyword variations. If two proposed pages answer the same decision with nearly identical proof, consolidate them.

Map the reader's next action before choosing an H1. Some pages need a booking CTA, others a quote form, a comparison table or simply a clear explanation. A content calendar that ignores the conversion path tends to generate traffic without useful enquiries.

Evidence that belongs in an Australian brief

For a plumbing company, gather actual service boundaries, licence details when relevant, call hours and what is included in a quote. For an Australian SaaS company, gather product documentation, integration limits, commercial-plan distinctions and tested screenshots. For a health provider, clinician approval and advertising-rule review are part of the work, not an optional editorial polish.

Australian English should be natural and consistent, but swapping 'optimization' for 'optimisation' does not make a page locally relevant. It needs accurate local terms, current rules where applicable, genuine operating details and sources the business can defend.

Brief fieldPractical instructionReviewer
Primary decisionWhat will a visitor know or do after reading?SEO strategist
First-hand factsBusiness-provided scope, fees, processes or product recordsBusiness owner
Required proofScreenshots, citations, quotes or documents authorised for useContent lead
Risky claimsHealth outcomes, prices, rebates, testimonials and guaranteesQualified reviewer
Acceptance testFactual accuracy, useful uniqueness, link targets, CTAAgency editor

Worked example: a dental clinic's teeth whitening page

Illustrative example, not clinical advice. The keyword set includes teeth whitening by suburb, whitening price and suitability questions. A thin content brief might ask for 900 words with three headings and a stock smile photo.

A useful brief instead requests practitioner-approved treatment descriptions, who provides the service, how suitability is assessed, aftercare topics the clinic is authorised to explain, actual pricing presentation and what the initial consultation includes. The writer must not promise a specific colour change or insert patient praise about treatment outcomes as advertising.

The acceptance check is whether the practitioner has signed off the treatment and outcome wording, the booking path works, and the page answers the intended patient questions without relying on unsupported superlatives. The Ahpra rules are a review gate, not a marketing talking point.

How a brief prevents scaled-content problems

Do not generate 'dentist in Suburb A' and 'dentist in Suburb B' as separate pages if the only change is the suburb name. Document what is genuinely different about the clinic's service, location, staff, access or patient journey. When the proposed pages do not have distinct value, update one useful service page and improve navigation instead.

The brief should include a 'do not write' field for unsupported claims and a source list. A reviewer should be able to reject a page that is smooth but empty. Search keywords are inputs to the editorial decision, not permission to create unlimited URLs.

What a complete content handoff contains

Return a title direction, intent and audience, recommended outline, unique evidence requirements, internal links, CTA, prohibited or unverified claims, and acceptance criteria. If a writer has already drafted the page, include specific revision notes instead of a generic 'make it SEO friendly' comment.

For recurring engagements, track percentage of briefs approved first pass, research questions returned to the client, revisions caused by incorrect business facts and pages actually published. A brief is complete when the designated editor can commission or approve the page without reconstructing the research.

  • A concise reader decision and intent map.
  • Evidence requests separated from verified facts.
  • Page-level outline and non-negotiable answers.
  • A claim review table where Australian rules may apply.
  • Internal linking and primary action tested in the draft.

Questions agencies ask before delegating this work

Does an SEO brief include the finished article?

Not automatically. The proposal should distinguish keyword research, brief production, drafting, editing, subject-matter review and publishing.

Can one brief be reused for multiple Australian cities?

Only when those pages genuinely have different user needs and facts. A different suburb name alone does not justify a separate page.

Who approves regulated content?

The client’s designated qualified reviewer. Outsourcing content production does not transfer responsibility for health, legal, financial or other regulated claims.

Shopify SEO Handoffs for Australian E-commerce Agencies

A Shopify SEO handoff should preserve the store's product information, collection intent and checkout journey. The technical work is different from generic WordPress SEO, especially when one store sells into several markets.

Get a Quote →View sample deliverables

A Shopify store can generate multiple paths to products through collections. It can also serve different prices, languages and catalogues in different markets. A checklist that only changes meta titles misses the architecture, market configuration and product information behind the store's search experience.

An agency may own theme development, paid acquisition and merchandising while outsourcing technical SEO checks. That boundary works when the scope names which changes require merchant approval and distinguishes search output from stock, product claims and checkout behaviour.

Start with how shoppers actually browse

Collection pages often serve discovery searches such as product type, material, use case or compatible device. Product pages serve a narrower decision about fit, features, delivery, returns and availability. The keyword map should follow those decisions. Two collections with almost identical products and copy may not need separate indexable pages.

Before proposing new filters or collections, look at the existing navigation, internal search terms, sales categories and the filters customers already use. Merchandising has consequences for crawlable URLs; a technical SEO recommendation should not quietly reorganise the catalogue without the merchant's sign-off.

Shopify-specific checks a handoff must cover

Shopify manages many technical elements automatically, including canonicals and market-specific signals, but theme customisation and third-party apps can change rendered output. Test actual URLs and structured data rather than assume the platform's default behaviour survived every installation.

A good handoff includes both the affected collection or product URLs and the level of change: theme code, content, Markets settings or an app. It should also show whether the change affects pricing, tracking or variant selection.

Shopify concernWhat to inspectAcceptance evidence
Collection-product pathsCanonical on products reachable from multiple collectionsRendered canonical matches the intended product URL
Faceted navigationWhether filtered URLs become useful landing pages or crawl clutterApproved indexation rules and working product discovery
MarketsTarget region, URL structure, language and currency contextMarket URL and hreflang/canonical settings reviewed
Product schemaPrice, availability, variants and review dataVisible product data agrees with validated markup
Out-of-stock productsWhether the product returns, is discontinued or has an alternativeMerchant-approved page handling and retained user journey

Worked example: one Australian store opens a New Zealand market

Illustrative case, not a client achievement. An Australian homewares store adds a New Zealand market. A marketer suggests copying every product into a separate NZ collection and writing a second description with country names replaced. The underlying offer is largely the same, but availability, delivery and currency details may differ.

Start by checking the Shopify Markets configuration and the URLs it actually generates. Verify the relevant market-specific page, local price and delivery disclosures. Shopify's documentation describes automatic canonicals and hreflang for market variants, but the site's live theme should still be inspected. Do not build another set of duplicate product pages merely to include 'New Zealand' in headings.

Accept the work when the market pages are discoverable as intended, the correct product and price context appears to the visitor, the canonical and hreflang settings are consistent and test checkouts route to the right market. Document any exception caused by an app or custom theme.

Merchandising and consumer claims are not optional SEO details

Australian product pages may include delivery estimates, savings claims, availability, reviews and warranty statements. The ACCC expects statements to be accurate and supported. An SEO editor should not invent a previous price, stock status, five-star endorsement or delivery window to fill a content gap.

The merchant is the source of truth for product facts. The agency can improve structure, comparison clarity and internal navigation while leaving commercial assertions to the people who can verify them.

A practical pilot scope for Shopify agencies

Choose one high-value collection, five representative product URLs and a single cross-market route if Markets is enabled. Run a crawl and rendered-page inspection, identify duplicated or misleading signals, then prepare only the changes that a developer or merchant can reasonably approve in that work cycle.

A white-label handoff should include the affected pages, tickets by ownership, source screenshots, approvals, deploy references, and a retest. If conversion tracking is in scope, test add-to-cart and purchase events in the proper environment rather than claim a technical page change improved revenue.

  • Agency controls merchant communication and brand promises.
  • SEO reviewer supplies priority decisions, page mapping and verification.
  • Developer manages theme, app and data changes with rollback.
  • Merchant confirms product data, market availability, returns and claims.

Decide when the existing ecommerce page is enough

A small store with one market and one simple collection structure may need a few technical tickets rather than a separate ongoing Shopify programme. Conversely, a large catalogue with complex filters and Markets rules warrants specialised QA. Scope should follow the site, not a preset quota of new collection pages.

Keep an explicit exclusion list: inventory synchronisation, theme redevelopment, feed management and paid-shopping configuration are separate responsibilities unless written into the agreement.

Questions agencies ask before delegating this work

Does Shopify automatically handle canonical URLs?

Shopify provides canonical and international SEO features, but rendered output can still be affected by themes and apps. Test the store's actual pages.

Should every filter create an indexed collection URL?

No. Keep indexable paths only when they serve a useful, distinct shopper need and can be maintained with accurate inventory and content.

Does this include revenue or conversion guarantees?

No. The SEO handoff includes technical checks and documented implementation acceptance. Commercial performance depends on product, pricing, merchandising, traffic and many other factors.
